text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I pushed a sketch for a per-layer precision policy + runtime fallback chain. Wanted to capture tradeoffs before I open a PR. PTAL

dmitri: Thanks — can you paste the minimal config here? curious how it maps to runtime decisions (batching, KV cache eviction, etc.)

maya: Sure, pasted below. Key ideas: a) explicit per-layer target (int4/int8/fp8/fp16), b) an ordered fallback list, c) a cheap "calib_hint" flag that triggers an optional micro-calibration on first warmup.

```json
{
  "precision_profile": "aggressive",
  "layer_policies": {
    "attn.k": "int4",
    "attn.v": "int8",
    "ffn.gate": "fp8",
    "embeddings": "fp16"
  },
  "fallback_chain": ["int4","int8","fp8","fp16"],
  "calib_hint": true
}
```

alex: Nice. Couple notes from runtime side: 1) int4 -> int8 fallback must preserve KV cache layout (we want same cache key shape so we can swap kernels mid-stream). 2) fallback that promotes to fp8 sometimes needs different packing; we should avoid triggering full model recompile on fallback.

maya: Right — I was thinking the runtime exposes a "precision adapter" interface that can swap kernels in-place if quant layout compatible, otherwise triggers a per-shard micro-recompile limited to that operator. That keeps most requests unaffected.

sara: We need clear eval gating. My worry: aggressive per-layer int4 will have tail cases with >2% quality regressions on instruction-following. We should: a) require an eval suite bound for each model-version+profile, b) auto-fail rollout if GIST response-regression > threshold, c) record per-prompt deltas to help debug.

maya: Agreed. Proposed rollout plan in PR: canary 0.5% with strict eval pass, then 5% with monitoring windows, then 25/100 staged. If regression detected -> auto rollback and mark the layer-policy as "unsafe" for that model.

bench-bot: perf snapshot (small testbed, batch=8, seq=512): int4 aggressive vs baseline fp16: latency p50: -22%, throughput: +47%, memory: -41%, reg metric delta: +0.9% (task: summarization set A)

dmitri: Those perf gains are compelling. Two tradeoffs to call out explicitly in the doc: 1) model artifact compatibility (we need metadata in the model store describing per-layer quantizable ranges), 2) billing/observability (because token costs change when we hit fallbacks).

alex: For (1) we can extend the model manifest with a simple per-tensor quant meta: min/max/scale/zero_point or a small histogram sample. Keep it optional for legacy models. For (2) runtime should emit events: `precision.used`, `precision.fallback`, and `precision.calibration` with minimal payload. Those are cheap and wire into console dashboards.

maya: I'm also proposing a conservative default: profile="safety-first" that prefers int8/fp8 and only uses int4 for embedding lookups where we've seen stable signals. "aggressive" is opt-in.

sara: Can we add a configuration knob to disable auto-fallback at customer request? Some enterprise customers want predictable exact behavior.

maya: Yes — privacy/enterprise flags: `allow_auto_fallback: true/false` and `fallback_policy: immediate|deferred|disabled`. Deferred = attempt warming then degrade gracefully.

alex: One more operational note: when fallback happens mid-request we should annotate the span and include a compact diff of which layers changed precision. That will make debugging much easier than perf-only traces. Keep payload tiny (layer names + from->to).

dmitri: Sounds good. I'll prototype the precision-adapter shim in the runtime repo and mock the events. Maya — want me to open the shim PR and add a test harness that simulates cache-compatible vs incompatible fallbacks?

maya: Yes please. I'll draft the RFC -> PR with config and rollout plan. Sara, can you add the eval thresholds you want into the PR?

sara: On it. I'll add a small eval harness plus alerting rules (1% auto-fail, 0.5% warning) and a checklist for canary telemetry.

maya: Great. Action items: dmitri prototype shim, sara add eval thresholds, alex add observability events + span annotation, bench-bot run medium suite on our staging harness and attach numbers to PR. I'll open PR end of day tomorrow. :rocket:

bench-bot: queued medium suite (batch=16, seq=2048) — ETA 2h :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: Minor naming suggestion: use `precision_profile` values like `conservative|balanced|aggressive` instead of freeform strings. Easier to document.

maya: Makes sense. I'll update the sketch. Thanks everyone.

bench-bot: medium suite results ready: throughput +38%, latency p50 -18%, memory -33%, reg delta +1.2% (longer context tests)
